entries.title: Nehemiah 11:1
Nehemiah 11:2
segments: Verse 2.  All the men that willingly offered]  Some volunteered their services, which was considered a sacrifice to patriotism at that time, as Jerusalem afforded very few advantages, and was a place of considerable danger; hence the people spoke well of them, and no doubt prayed for God's blessing upon them.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:3
segments: Verse 3.  Now these are the chief]  A good deal of difference will be found between the enumeration here and that in
, &c.  There, those only who came with Zerubbabel appear to be numbered; here, those, and the persons who came with Ezra and Nehemiah, enter into the account.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:9
segments: Verse 9.  And Joel-was their overseer]  Joel was chief or magistrate over those, and Judah was his second or deputy. Perhaps each had a different office, but that of Joel was the chief.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:11
segments: Verse 11.  Ruler of the house of God.]  He had the command over all secular matters, as the high priest had over those which were spiritual.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:14
segments: Verse 14.  Mighty men of valour]  Noted for strength of body, and military courage.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:16
segments:
Verse 16.  And Shabbethai]  This verse, with verses 20, 21, 28, 29, 32, 33, 34, and 35, are all wanting in the Septuagint and the whole chapter is wanting in the Arabic, the translator not being concerned in Jewish genealogies. 
 
  The outward business]  Calmet supposes that he provided the victuals for the priests, victims for the sacrifices, the sacerdotal vestments, the sacred vessels, and other necessaries for the service of the temple.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:17
segments: Verse 17.  The principal to begin the thanksgiving]  The precentor, pitcher of the tune, or master-singer.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:22
segments: Verse 22.  The overseer also of the Levites]  dyqp pekid, the visitant, the inspector; translated episkopov, bishop, both by the Septuagint and Vulgate.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:23
segments: Verse 23.  It was the king's commandment]  By the king some understand David, and others Artaxerxes.  It is most probable that it was the latter; who wished that a provision should be made for these, a part of whose office was to offer up prayers also, as well as praises.  For we know that Darius made an ample provision for the priests, that they might offer sacrifices of sweet savour unto the God of heaven; and pray for the life of the king and of his sons,
.  Some have thought that they had been Jewish singers employed in the service of the Persian king, to whom he had given a salary, and to whom he wished still to continue the same.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:24
segments: Verse 24.  Pethahiah-was at the king's hand]  He was the governor appointed by the Persian king over the Jewish nation in those matters in which the civil government interfered with Jewish concerns.  He no doubt fixed, levied, and received the tribute.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:26
segments: Verse 26.  And at Jeshua]  This city is nowhere else mentioned.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:28
segments: Verse 28.  Mekonah]  This city is also unknown.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:31
segments: Verse 31.  Geba]  Probably the same as Gibeah of Saul.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:32
segments: Verse 32.  Ananiah]  No city of this name is known.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:33
segments:
Verse 33.  Hadid]  This place is also unknown. 
 
  Neballat]  Also unknown.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:35
segments: Verse 35.  Lod, and Ono]  These towns were built by the sons of Elpaal,

. 
 
  The valley of craftsmen.]  See
.  Probably this latter town was built in this valley.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:36
segments:
Verse 36.  And of the Levites were divisions]  The Levites had their dwellings in the divisions of Judah and Benjamin.  This is probably the meaning: the Syriac says, They had the half of Judah and Benjamin; which is not likely. 
 
THAT the people whose hearts were now turned towards the Lord, would make the best provision for the support of God's work, and all those engaged in it, we may naturally suppose; but this could not be very great, as the complete service was not yet established, and the Levites themselves were few in number.
